blocks.text: LEGAZPI CITY — Fourteen whales and dolphins have found their final resting place at a cemetery in Bula, Camarines Sur, maintained by the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) in Bicol. Established in 2013, the BFAR-5 Cetacean Cemetery is located within the agency’s regional office compound in Barangay Fabrica. It serves as a burial ground for marine mammals found stranded or dead along the region’s coastlines. The 14 animals buried at the site include Risso’s dolphins, spinner dolphins, Fraser’s dolphins, striped dolphins, a dwarf sperm whale and a Bryde’s whale.
